claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is modeled as a disordered random solid solution with realistic atomic-scale disorder.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal conductivities of disordered HfNbTaTiZr are of comparable magnitude.
Above 300 K, disorder-induced phonon scattering significantly reduces lattice thermal conductivity relative to the electronic contribution.
The predicted total thermal conductivity above 300 K will fall within 10–17 W/(K m).
The proposed framework will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 20–30% relative to previous models.
MBPT combined with TDEP can extract temperature- and disorder-modified phonon dispersions, force constants, vibrational spectra, and electron–phonon coupling parameters for HfNbTaTiZr.
The Kubo–Greenwood formalism can be used to calculate the electronic and phonon thermal-conductivity contributions separately.
TDEP-derived force constants and vibrational spectra represent alloy disorder and determine phonon lifetimes and scattering rates.
MBPT provides electron–phonon coupling parameters sensitive to the local atomic environment.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by disorder lowers the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
Electron–phonon interactions modulate the electronic heat-transport channel.
Computing and then summing independent lattice and electronic contributions will better capture the alloy's atomistic complexity than earlier approaches.
At high temperature, impurity scattering and disorder effects become dominant.
Previous relevant simulations treated perfect or defect-free crystals.
Previous approaches conflated lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Some previous analytical conductivity estimates require a Debye temperature.
The framework is applicable to bulk, random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr over 100–1200 K, optionally with 1 wt.% oxygen.
Reliability is limited by disorder sampling, convergence of many-body effects, computational expense, temperature extremes, and heterogeneous impurity distributions.
Combined TDTR with frequency-domain modulation can separately quantify phonon and electronic thermal conductivity up to 1200 K.

contradictions.description: The claimed 20–30% improvement changes meaning across fields: it is first an improvement in predictive accuracy, then a reduction in prediction uncertainty, and finally a deviation in uncertainty. These are distinct metrics and are not interchangeable without a defined benchmark.
